title: Per-tooth MSC cells: rescue tooth-tip maxima from over-smoothing
description:
After PATCH-28 boundary snap, the SCALAR overlay still shows high Coons error across the teeth (yellow/orange band on both upper and lower jaws), and FLAT view shows all upper teeth in one cell + all lower teeth in another. The MSC ascending-manifold can only produce one cell per retained MAX critical point. With 50 iterations of Laplacian smoothing on the scalar field plus persistence-pairing culling (MorseSmaleComplex.java), each row of teeth fuses into a single max — the per-tooth tips disappear. PATCH-28 can route boundaries onto interdental crest lines but it can't conjure a cell where there's no max. Without per-tooth cells, no Coons-fit will ever be tight on the teeth area no matter how good the boundary snap is.

**Progress 2026-04-25 (per-tooth maxima rescued, Coons fits still loose).** Smoothing iterations exposed as parameters on MorseSmaleComplex.compute (50/30 default unchanged for back-compat) and threaded through SemanticPatchDecomposer. MorseSmaleDecomposer now uses 25/20 → tooth-tip maxima survive into the critical-point set; Coons error vector is recomputed against the new MSC patches (replaces the borrowed-from-semantic stale vector that masked the failure). Visual: bottom-view shows distinct cells along both upper and lower dental arches. Numbers on voyage_skull_ref.obj at 35/25: total cells 66→97 (within 1.5× cap), tooth-region cells (top-10% mean-H proxy) 2→38, tooth-region Coons p50 ≈ 0.10 (right at threshold 0.114), tooth-region Coons p95 ≈ 0.28 (still above threshold). The p95 failure is structural: many tooth cells are not 4-sided so CoonsReconstructionError skips them, and per-vertex error reflects the worst neighbour cell. Closing the p95 gap requires PATCH-29 (formal quad-cell topology) — 32 + 29 should be evaluated together. Files: MorseSmaleComplex.java, SemanticPatchDecomposer.java, MorseSmaleDecomposer.java.
definition-of-done: Each tooth on the skull becomes its own MSC cell (or at least each pair of incisors / each molar becomes its own cell). Concretely: after running on voyage_skull_ref.obj, lower jaw should have ≥6 distinct cells along the dental arch instead of one. Approaches to evaluate: (a) reduce smoothing iterations on the input scalar from 50 → 10-20 and re-tune saddle threshold; (b) use a different scalar (curvature-driven rather than the current height/displacement field); (c) lower the persistence-pairing threshold so low-but-real tooth-tip maxima are retained; (d) run a local re-detection pass restricted to high-Coons-error cells to find sub-maxima. Pick whichever gives clean per-tooth cells without exploding cell count elsewhere.
testing-plan: 1) Run VerifyMsDecomposer on skull; expected ≥6 cells along the lower dental arch. 2) Coons p95 error in the teeth region drops below T_COONS_ERROR_FRAC * meshExtent (0.025 × extent). 3) Other anatomical regions (cranium, orbit, nasal) keep cell counts within 20% of the post-PATCH-28 baseline (66 cells) — i.e. fix shouldn't cause a fragmentation explosion elsewhere. 4) Visual check in viewer: each tooth has its own color in FLAT mode.
